newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco's UMT group denounces Renault layoffs.
newsitem.headline: Morocco's UMT group denounces Renault layoffs.

text.p: Morocco's largest Union Marocaine du Travail (UMT) on Tuesday denounced the decision by French car maker Renault SA to shut down its plant in Belgium and axe 3,000 workers, including some North Africans.

"UMT has expressed its solidarity with workers and denounced Renault's management decision to dismiss thousands of employees in the name of world globalisation and savage economic competitiveness," the Casablanca-based union said in a statement.

UMT, which has sent a letter of protest to Renault management in Belgium, said: "The company did not take into account the social aspect of the problem and other negative impacts of closing the car plants."

Last month Renault conceded that it was in serious trouble and said it would close a high-cost plant at Vilvoorde in Belgium which employs 3,100 people. It will also accelerate its job-reduction programme in France, cutting 2,764 jobs in 1997 after 1,640 last year from a total workforce of near 141,000.

An independent union group, UMT is the country's largest with more than half a million affiliated workers. The two other groups are Confederation Democratique du Travail and Union Generale des Travailleurs Marocains, both linked to opposition parties.
